title: U.S. House · Wisconsin's 2nd Congressional District
area: South-central Wisconsin, including Madison and surrounding Dane County.

context.text: No candidate filed for the Republican primary in this district. Incumbent Mark Pocan (D) defeated Douglas Alexander in the Democratic primary and is unopposed on the November 3 general election ballot.

candidates.name: Mark Pocan
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated Douglas Alexander in the Democratic primary; unopposed in the general election.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's 2nd Congressional District (since 2013)

summary.text: Mark Pocan is the Democratic incumbent for Wisconsin's 2nd Congressional District, which he has represented since 2013. A Kenosha native, he owned a printing business, served on the Dane County Board of Supervisors, and spent 14 years in the Wisconsin State Assembly. He serves on the House Appropriations and Foreign Affairs committees and is Chair Emeritus of the Congressional Progressive Caucus.

background.text: Born in Kenosha, Wisconsin, in 1964 (August 14, per Wikipedia), and raised there; graduated from Mary D. Bradford High School in 1982.
Earned a bachelor's degree in journalism from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1986.
Opened and owned Budget Signs & Specialties, a printing business, after graduating; his House biography describes him as a former small business owner and union member.
Served on the Dane County Board of Supervisors from 1991 to 1996.

Elected to the Wisconsin State Assembly in 1998 to succeed Tammy Baldwin, and served until 2013; sat on the Joint Finance Committee for six years, including a term as co-chair, according to Wikipedia.
Sworn in as U.S. Representative on January 3, 2013, succeeding Baldwin after she was elected to the U.S. Senate.

In the 119th Congress sits on the House Appropriations Committee (Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies; Financial Services and General Government subcommittees) and the House Foreign Affairs Committee.

Chaired the Congressional Progressive Caucus from 2017 to 2021 (alongside Pramila Jayapal), according to Wikipedia, and is now its Chair Emeritus; co-chairs the Congressional Equality Caucus and co-founded and co-chairs the Labor Caucus and the Defense Spending Reduction Caucus.

priorities.text: Says he is committed to investing in education to give future generations the tools to become leaders.
Says the budget should strengthen Social Security and Medicare and invest in job growth through infrastructure, education, and research while reducing deficits.
Says he opposes discrimination in all forms and has fought as co-chair of the Congressional LGBTQ+ Equality Caucus to end it.

positions.summary: Says he believes the country must continue to expand and innovate within the healthcare system to provide all Wisconsinites access to health insurance that meets their needs.
Says making the country more energy efficient will reduce the carbon footprint and position the U.S. to thrive in a twenty-first-century economy.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations, including the Financial Services and General Government and Labor-HHS-Education subcommittees, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Co-chairs the Congressional LGBTQ+ Equality Caucus.
